question: Should OpenClaw support `agents.defaults.compaction.enabled` as a durable public switch for threshold-driven embedded auto-compaction while retaining overflow recovery and manual compaction behavior?
rationale: The implementation is narrow and keeps existing unset configurations enabled, but it converts an internal/runtime setting into a documented long-term configuration contract.

options.title: Accept the public setting
options.body: Merge the optional boolean with its current default-true behavior and documented limited scope.

options.title: Keep the control internal
options.body: Decline the new public config contract and instead direct users to an existing supported compaction control or a separately designed operator workflow.

recommendation.title: Accept the public setting
recommendation.body: Merge the optional boolean with its current default-true behavior and documented limited scope.
